findings.title: Cleanup jobs now run ten times more often
findings.body: This changes the interval for the entire cleanup service from 10 minutes to 1 minute, so every cleanup job—not just annotation cleanup—runs ten times as frequently. That increases recurring database and filesystem work and can create unnecessary load; keep the existing interval unless this broader scheduling change is intentional.

findings.title: Building large ID lists repeatedly copies the growing string
findings.body: For SQLite batches above the parameter limit, each iteration formats a new string containing the entire list accumulated so far. This is quadratic in the number of IDs and can copy hundreds of megabytes for a batch of tens of thousands, making the large-batch cleanup path—and the added large-batch integration test—needlessly slow and allocation-heavy. Build the list with a builder or join formatted values once.

findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged at error level with every ID
findings.body: This logs ordinary cleanup progress as an error, including the full ID list, and the same pattern is used for count-based and orphan-tag cleanup. It can flood error monitoring and logs during normal operation, especially with large batches; use a lower log level and avoid logging every ID.
